issues.legal_issue: Under a Hindu will giving two beneficiaries a shared life interest, the beneficiaries take as tenants in common rather than joint tenants unless the will provides for survivorship or they are coparceners in an undivided family.
material_facts: The childless testatrix brought up two foster children from infancy and made a will giving both possession and enjoyment of her property for their lifetimes, without power to alienate it.
The will did not expressly provide that on the death of one beneficiary the property would pass to the other by survivorship.
The beneficiaries were not coparceners in an undivided family and later partitioned the property between themselves.
issues.conclusion: The beneficiaries took the life interests as tenants in common, not as joint tenants.
issues.legal_principle: In Jogeswar Narain Deo v. Ram Chund Dutt (23 I.A. 37) and Babu Rani v. Rajendra Baksh Singh (60 I.A. 95), the Privy Council stated that joint tenancy is unknown to Hindu law except for coparcenary among members of an undivided family. A technical English rule of joint tenancy should not be imported into the construction of a Hindu will. The terms of this will did not provide for survivorship.

rule.if: hindu_will_construction and shared_life_possession and beneficiaries_not_family_coparceners and no_survivorship_direction

predicates.hindu_will_construction: The proceeding requires construction of a will governed by Hindu law.
predicates.shared_life_possession: The will gives multiple beneficiaries shared possession or enjoyment of property for their lifetimes.
predicates.beneficiaries_not_family_coparceners: The beneficiaries are not coparceners in an undivided family.
predicates.no_survivorship_direction: The will does not direct that the surviving beneficiary takes the deceased beneficiary's interest by survivorship.

issues.definition: When a Hindu will gives multiple non-coparcener beneficiaries shared lifetime enjoyment without directing survivorship, they hold their life interests as tenants in common.

issues.legal_issue: Where a will gives several beneficiaries life interests and gives the remainder to their children after the respective beneficiaries' deaths, those children take per stirpes rather than per capita.
material_facts: The testatrix brought up two foster children as her own and, while they were minors, gave them the property for their lifetimes without powers of gift, transfer or sale.
The will directed that after the beneficiaries' deaths, the children born to them would enjoy the property with powers of ownership.
The beneficiaries were to have separate interests in the property, and the will provided for their children to succeed to those interests.
issues.conclusion: The children of the beneficiaries take the remainder per stirpes, succeeding to the respective interest of their own parent, rather than taking equal shares per capita.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the rule that a gift to several persons for life followed by a gift to their children or issue is construed as taking effect on each parent's death in favour of that parent's issue, so that the issue take the share to which that parent was entitled. The court relied on the construction in In re Hutchinson's Trusts (21 Ch. D. 811), Errington, In re: Gibbs v. Lassam ([1927] 1 Ch. 421), and McDonnell v. Neil ([1951] A.C. 342), and referred to Halsbury's Laws of England, vol. 39, 3rd ed., art. 1638. The terms and circumstances of the will also supported the inference that each foster child was to enjoy half the income for life and that their children were to succeed to their respective interests.

rule.if: construction_of_will and life_interests_given_to_multiple_beneficiaries and remainder_given_to_their_children and succession_tied_to_each_parent

predicates.construction_of_will: The proceeding requires construction of a will.
predicates.life_interests_given_to_multiple_benefic: The will gives multiple beneficiaries interests lasting for their respective lifetimes.
predicates.remainder_given_to_their_children: The will gives the property after the life interests to the beneficiaries' children.
predicates.succession_tied_to_each_parent: The will or its circumstances connect each child's succession to the interest of that child's own parent.

issues.definition: When a will gives multiple beneficiaries life interests and connects the remainder for their children to each parent's interest, those children take per stirpes.
